title.es: Señalizar el recorrido de una charla

es: Reconocer y ordenar las expresiones que señalizan la apertura, las transiciones, los desvíos y el cierre de una charla, y elegir la fórmula adecuada para cada momento.

teaching.en: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for coming: today I will present the results of our neighbourhood survey, which reached more than six hundred households.
teaching.es: Buenos días a todos y gracias por venir: hoy presentaré los resultados de nuestra encuesta del barrio, que llegó a más de seiscientos hogares.
teaching.explanationEs: Apertura: saludo + agradecimiento + I will present… anuncia el tema y un dato sitúa al público.
segments: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for coming: today I will present the
results of our neighbourhood survey, which reached more than six hundred households.
teaching.audioText: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for coming: today I will present the results of our neighbourhood survey, which reached more than six hundred households.

teaching.en: I will outline the talk in three parts, and firstly I will explain how we collected the data, before I turn to what residents told us.
teaching.es: Expondré la charla en tres partes y, en primer lugar, explicaré cómo recogimos los datos, antes de pasar a lo que nos dijeron los vecinos.
teaching.explanationEs: I will outline… anuncia el esquema; firstly abre la primera parte y before… deja ver la siguiente.
segments: I will outline the talk in three parts, and firstly I will explain
how we collected the data, before I turn to what residents told us.
teaching.audioText: I will outline the talk in three parts, and firstly I will explain how we collected the data, before I turn to what residents told us.

teaching.en: Now that the method is clear, let's move on to the results, and I will touch on the most surprising figures only briefly.
teaching.es: Ahora que el método está claro, pasemos a los resultados, y mencionaré solo de pasada las cifras más sorprendentes.
teaching.explanationEs: Let's move on to + parte es la transición habitual; touch on = tratar algo por encima, sin detenerse.
segments: Now that the method is clear, let's move on to the results,
and I will touch on the most surprising figures only briefly.
teaching.audioText: Now that the method is clear, let's move on to the results, and I will touch on the most surprising figures only briefly.

teaching.en: Good speakers signpost every stage of a talk, and if they digress, they say so openly and return to the main point.
teaching.es: Los buenos oradores señalizan cada etapa de una charla y, si se desvían del tema, lo dicen abiertamente y vuelven al punto principal.
teaching.explanationEs: Signpost es el verbo de marcar el camino al público; digress = apartarse del tema, y se avisa.
segments: Good speakers signpost every stage of a talk, and if they
digress, they say so openly and return to the main point.
teaching.audioText: Good speakers signpost every stage of a talk, and if they digress, they say so openly and return to the main point.

teaching.en: Now I'd like to turn to the question of noise, which worried more residents than any other issue in our survey.
teaching.es: Ahora me gustaría pasar al tema del ruido, que preocupó a más vecinos que cualquier otro asunto de nuestra encuesta.
teaching.explanationEs: Now I'd like to turn to + tema: transición algo más formal; el tema va con the question of…
segments: Now I'd like to turn to the question of noise, which
worried more residents than any other issue in our survey.
teaching.audioText: Now I'd like to turn to the question of noise, which worried more residents than any other issue in our survey.

teaching.en: To sum up, most neighbours want safer streets and quieter nights; finally, I will be glad to take any questions you may have.
teaching.es: En resumen, la mayoría de los vecinos quiere calles más seguras y noches más tranquilas; por último, responderé con gusto a las preguntas que tengan.
teaching.explanationEs: Cierre: To sum up + idea principal; finally anuncia el último paso y take questions abre el turno de preguntas.
segments: To sum up, most neighbours want safer streets and quieter nights; finally,
I will be glad to take any questions you may have.
teaching.audioText: To sum up, most neighbours want safer streets and quieter nights; finally, I will be glad to take any questions you may have.

prompt.es: ¿Qué función cumple este fragmento dentro de una charla?

choices.text: It moves the audience on from the method to the results.
It sums up the conclusions before the final questions.
It opens the talk and announces how it will be organised.

feedback.es: El saludo, «I will outline» y «firstly» forman una apertura: anuncian el esquema. Una transición usaría move on to y un cierre, to sum up.

hint.es: Fíjate en el saludo inicial y en «I will outline»: ¿abre, enlaza o cierra?

origin.text: Good morning, everyone. Over the next ten minutes I will outline three findings from our neighbourhood survey, and firstly I want to explain why we asked these questions at all.

prompt.es: Completa: «Ahora me gustaría pasar al tema del ruido.»

feedback.es: Turn to + tema es la transición formal para cambiar de parte; el verbo turn va seguido de to.

hint.es: Es el verbo que también significa «girar».

origin.text: We have covered the method, so the audience is ready for the next part. Now I'd like to ___ to the question of noise, which worries residents more than anything else.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Por último, responderé con gusto a sus preguntas.»

answer.text: Finally I will be happy to take your questions

feedback.es: Finally anuncia el último paso de la charla y take questions es la fórmula que abre el turno de preguntas.

hint.es: Empieza con Finally y termina con las preguntas.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué hizo la oradora a mitad de la charla.

choices.text: She told a personal story, then went back to her point.
She skipped the method and moved directly to the results.
She asked the council to vote on her proposal.

feedback.es: A mitad de la charla se desvió con una anécdota de su calle, lo avisó y volvió al punto principal.

origin.audio: Last week I watched my cousin give a talk on the results of a neighbourhood survey. She opened with a joke, then outlined three parts: how the survey was carried out, what residents said about noise and traffic, and what she thinks the council should do. Halfway through, she digressed into a story about her own street, but she said so openly, apologised and returned to her main point. She finished with a short summary and invited questions.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada fórmula del orador con lo que hace en la charla.

pairs: I'd like to begin by outlining how the talk is organised.

pairs.es: anuncia el esquema de la charla

pairs: If I may digress for a moment, let me tell you about my street.

pairs.es: abre un paréntesis avisando al público

pairs: I'll touch on parking only briefly, since few people mentioned it.
To sum up, residents want quieter nights and safer crossings.

feedback.es: Cada fórmula cumple un papel: anunciar el esquema, avisar de un desvío, tratar algo de pasada o cerrar con una síntesis.

pairs: I'd like to begin by outlining how the talk is organised.

pairs.es: anuncia el esquema de la charla

pairs: If I may digress for a moment, let me tell you about my street.

pairs.es: abre un paréntesis avisando al público

pairs: I'll touch on parking only briefly, since few people mentioned it.
To sum up, residents want quieter nights and safer crossings.

prompt.es: ¿Qué carencia señala sobre todo el comentario de la colega?

choices.text: Too many figures and too little explanation of them.
Too few signposts to show the plan and the ending.
A closing summary that was much too long for the talk.

feedback.es: No sabía adónde iba la charla y el final la sorprendió: faltaban señales (signposts) que marcaran el plan y el cierre.

origin.text: A colleague's feedback on a rehearsal: “Your facts were strong, but the talk felt like a list. I never knew where you were heading, and your last two minutes came as a complete surprise.”

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué prioridad sugiere el plan de la oradora.

choices.text: Parking and noise matter equally, so both get the same time.
The method is the main topic, with noise as a short extra.
Noise needs most of the time; parking very little.

feedback.es: Dedica una parte al ruido y menciona el estacionamiento solo de pasada porque pocos vecinos lo plantearon: el ruido es la prioridad.

origin.audio: At the residents' meeting, the speaker began by thanking everyone and promised to outline her findings in three parts. She would explain the method first, turn to noise next, and touch on parking only briefly, since few people had raised it. She added that she might digress once or twice, but would always say so before returning to her main point. Last, she said, she would take questions.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige por qué avisa de que quizá se desvíe.

choices.text: To keep the audience oriented even if she leaves her main line.
To excuse herself in advance for being badly prepared.
To warn everyone that the survey results are unreliable.

feedback.es: Avisar antes de desviarse y volver al punto principal ayuda al público a no perderse; no es una disculpa ni una duda sobre los datos.

origin.audio: At the residents' meeting, the speaker began by thanking everyone and promised to outline her findings in three parts. She would explain the method first, turn to noise next, and touch on parking only briefly, since few people had raised it. She added that she might digress once or twice, but would always say so before returning to her main point. Last, she said, she would take questions.

prompt.es: Completa: «Mencionaría el costo solo de pasada y se centraría en el ruido.»

feedback.es: Touch on significa mencionar un tema sin detenerse en él; encaja con «only briefly» y con el informe que ya lo detalla.

origin.text: Her plan was clear from the start. She would ___ on the cost only briefly, because the report covers it in detail, and then spend most of the time on noise.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Déjame hacer un paréntesis y luego volveré al punto.»

answer.text: Let me digress for a moment and then return to the point

feedback.es: Digress for a moment avisa del desvío y return to the point anuncia que el orador volverá al hilo principal.

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud muestra la oradora ante quienes pedían más detalle sobre el costo?

choices.text: She ignores the concern because cost is not her topic.
She accepts the complaint and offers to deal with it afterwards.
She promises an exact figure for every question asked.

feedback.es: Reconoce la queja («I realise…»), se ofrece a volver sobre ello y admite que quizá no tenga todas las cifras: ni la descarta ni promete lo imposible.

origin.text: So, to sum up: most residents want quieter nights, fewer cars and safer crossings. I realise some of you wanted more detail on the cost, and I'm happy to come back to that. Finally, I will take questions, although I may not have every figure to hand.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hará la oradora justo después de esa transición.

choices.text: Explain in detail why noise matters to residents.
Go back to the method to justify the sample.
Comment briefly on the wording of the question.

feedback.es: «First, though» anuncia un paso previo: antes de explicar por qué importa el ruido, hará un comentario breve sobre cómo formularon la pregunta.

origin.audio: Right, that covers how we ran the survey, so let me move on to the results. Nearly two thirds of people mentioned noise, and I will come back to why that matters. First, though, a quick word about how we worded the question, because it changes what the numbers mean.

prompt.es: Completa: «En primer lugar, quiero explicar cómo recogimos los datos.»

feedback.es: Firstly abre la primera parte anunciada en el esquema, justo después de saludar y presentar la estructura.

origin.text: She had rehearsed carefully. After greeting the audience and outlining the structure, she said: “___, I want to explain how we collected the data.”
